title: Push declined, and a hotfix gone missing

source.title: Remove sensitive files and their commits from Git history (Stack Overflow)

brief:
**#shop-deploy · 09:02**

> **dev:** my push of the rate-limit change is rejected: `push declined ... contains .env`. Can someone just turn the hook off? We need rate limiting before the 10:00 sale.

> **night shift:** also, where did my hotfix go? On Sunday at 23:41 I checked out `v1.4` on the server, raised `proxy_read_timeout` to 30s, committed, switched back to main... and now it's not in `git log`. INC-977 is back.

The repo is `/home/deploy/shop` (origin: `/srv/git/shop.git`), owned by `deploy`: work as `sudo -iu deploy`. Keep the hook. Ship both changes to origin/main without the secret and without losing anyone's work.

tasks.title: Get the secret out, ship the change
tasks.text:
Look at the last commit (`git show --stat`): it added the rate limit **and** `.env` with a database password. That commit was never pushed, so you can rewrite it safely.

Remove `.env` from the commit but keep the file on disk (the app reads it), make git ignore it for every clone, and push. Done when origin/main has `rate_limit=100`, no branch, tag or origin commit contains `.env`, and `.env` is still in the working tree but untracked and ignored.
hints: `git rm --cached .env` removes it from the index and leaves the file. Add `.env` to `.gitignore` and `git add .gitignore`.
`git commit --amend --no-edit` replaces the last commit with the cleaned one, then `git push origin main`. A password that was ever pushed or shared must be rotated as well.

questions.prompt: Which committed file makes git ignore `.env` in every clone?
Which git command removes a file from the index but keeps it on disk?

checks.describe: origin/main has the rate limit, no commit carries .env, .env is kept, untracked and ignored

tasks.title: Find the lost hotfix
tasks.text:
Checking out a tag puts you on a **detached HEAD**: new commits belong to no branch. When you switch away, nothing points to them any more. They are not deleted yet, though: git records every position of HEAD.

Find the hotfix commit, bring it onto `main` without losing the rate-limit work, and push. Done when `main` and origin/main both contain the hotfix commit and `timeout.conf` says 30s.
hints: `git reflog` lists where HEAD has been, newest first. Look for the line with "hotfix" and note its short hash. `git show <hash>` confirms it.
On main: `git cherry-pick <hash>` (or `git branch hotfix-977 <hash>` and merge it), then `git push origin main`.

questions.prompt: Which git command lists where HEAD has been, including commits no branch points to?
What is the state called when you commit on a checked-out tag?

checks.describe: main and origin/main contain the hotfix (30s) next to the rate limit

walkthrough:
### What was broken
1. The commit "Add rate limiting" also added `.env` (database password). The server's `pre-receive` hook rejects any push containing `.env`, like GitHub/GitLab push protection.
2. The hotfix was committed on a **detached HEAD** (`git checkout v1.4`). After `git checkout main`, no branch pointed to it. Only the reflog still listed it.

### Task 1
```bash
sudo -iu deploy
cd ~/shop
git status ; git log --oneline -3 ; git show --stat HEAD     # .env | 3 +++
git push origin main                                         # push declined ... contains .env
git rm --cached .env                                         # untrack, keep the file
echo .env >> .gitignore && git add .gitignore
git commit --amend --no-edit                                 # rewrite the unpushed commit
git push origin main
git check-ignore -v .env ; ls -l .env                        # .gitignore:1:.env  .env
```
*Why:* rewriting is safe only for commits nobody else has. Once a secret has been pushed or shared, removing it from history (`git filter-repo`, BFG) is not enough: **rotate the secret**, because clones, forks and caches keep copies.

### Task 2
```bash
git reflog | head -8          # ... checkout: moving from 1a2b3c4 to main
                              # 1a2b3c4 HEAD@{2}: commit: hotfix: raise proxy_read_timeout to 30s (INC-977)
git show 1a2b3c4              # timeout.conf 10s -> 30s
git cherry-pick 1a2b3c4       # copy it onto main
git push origin main
git log --oneline -3 ; cat timeout.conf
```
*Why:* the reflog is local and expires (by default unreachable entries after 30 days, then `git gc` deletes the objects), so rescue lost commits soon. Next time, make a branch before committing: `git switch -c hotfix-977 v1.4`.

**Source (adapted):** [Remove sensitive files and their commits from Git history](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/872565/remove-sensitive-files-and-their-commits-from-git-history): the answers stress that a pushed secret must be treated as compromised and changed. For the newest, unpushed commit, `git rm --cached` plus `git commit --amend` is enough.
